scope: Phase 2, smooth baseline versus lossless active-atlas scissors and populated upload ranges. Source runtime in Storybook; not a physical-device measurement or a published package comparison.
candidateNotes: First57 pixel snapshots measured the scissor/upload implementation before the host-only getContext compatibility fix committed with824f9457. Host omitted: normal web path. Latest controller extraction was also exercised in the final lifecycle gates.

All timing samples use unchanged asset geometry, lights, shaders, animation, MSAA4 offscreen target and60fps frame limit. CSS64/128/320 with DPR2 is tested at the existing renderer backing resolution, not an increased quality setting.
Controller extraction gates rerun at213c18c2: final shared reconciler preserves the same shader/render path.

pixelFidelity.method: Full viewport PNG screenshots from fixed held poses, exact RGBA equality inside every actively presented logical cell, including edges. Inactive atlas storage is intentionally excluded; destination retained canvas immutability is checked by the editor lifecycle gate.
inputs: idle before and after deferred work loading

hardwareControl.environment: Windows headless Chrome156, RTX5090 ANGLE D3D11, connected to dedicated test browser. This is a powerful GPU control, not a representative office or low-end device.
hardwareControl.gpuTimingMethod: EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2, asynchronous availability polling, discard disjoint samples. Per-render-pass queries include uploads, GL command issue gaps and the color pass MSAA resolve; they do not isolate shader execution. Query instrumentation adds overhead.

hardwareControl.interpretation: Both versions maintain about60fps. In64 fully active avatars, upload bytes, atlas area and GPU depth median are essentially unchanged. Sparse workloads reduce submitted upload bytes and scissored pixels; do not infer a universal all-active speedup from the first24-avatar pair.

softwareRenderer.environment: Linux headless Chrome146, ANGLE SwiftShader Vulkan software rendering; not a physical weak PC or phone. No CPU throttling.
softwareRenderer.interpretation: Strong host/software variance. Initial2s-warm DPR1 pair58.9→40.3fps did not reproduce: reversed5s-warm pair both60fps. DPR2 repeated before30.66/14.47 versus after60.02/46.63fps supports a directional benefit under pixel pressure, not a stable multiplier or real-device guarantee. Team builds were coordinated away from measured samples; unrelated repositories were not isolated. Later process inspection found concurrent external TypeScript/Rust jobs, so global quiet cannot be established. A brief team Metro compile during finalafter startup ended before the5s warmup/sample window.
softwareRenderer.cpuCaveat: DevTools TaskDuration and synchronous drawImage include waiting for rendering; these are not total-system CPU consumption. Software GPU process CPU is not included.

editorPool.scope: Real WebGL retained canvas, sparse middle slot, paused recolor, offscreen/resume, work lifecycle, failure and disposal.
editorPool.heldResizeClock: Exact work motionTime held across resolution/LOD promotion; original live one-cycle assertion could expire during software shader compilation.

lazyWork.execution: Seven original cases plus isolated new no-op/latest case; exact union equals script default eight scenarios.

reproduce.pixels: Capture baseline with BLOOM_STORYBOOK_URL and AVATAR_EQUIVALENCE_OUTPUT; run candidate with AVATAR_EQUIVALENCE_REFERENCE pointing to that folder. node scripts/verify-avatar-render-equivalence.mjs. Keep both origins and browser unchanged.
reproduce.timing: node scripts/measure-avatar-pool.mjs; AVATAR_POOL_COUNTS, AVATAR_POOL_SIZE, AVATAR_POOL_DPR, AVATAR_POOL_MODES, AVATAR_WARMUP_MS and AVATAR_SAMPLE_MS configure the workload. AVATAR_GPU_PROFILE=passes or resolve requires hardware timer extension; AVATAR_CPU_PROFILE=1 saves a cpuprofile. Run sequentially without other benchmarks/builds.
reproduce.apiCensus: node scripts/profile-avatar-gl-api.mjs records exact forwarded WebGL calls during startup, idle, prepareWork, work and dispose. This instrumentation is separate from timings.

webglApiCensus.note: Native backend requires actual API capability parity, including multisampled RGBA8/depth renderbuffers, framebuffer blit, float pose textures and instancing. An API name stub does not establish compatibility.
